q: A finance officer is reviewing the annual results of a zonal railway whose gross earnings for the year are Rs 5,000 crore and whose working expenses are Rs 4,400 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway for the year works out to:
e: Operating Ratio is working expenses expressed as a percentage of gross earnings. Here it is 4400 / 5000 x 100 = 88 per cent.

q: A patient travelling to a distant hospital for treatment of cancer, and for his periodic check-up thereafter, asks the booking clerk whether any concession in rail fare is admissible to him. The correct position is that concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: Only attendants accompanying a patient, and not to the patient himself
options.B: All persons travelling for a routine medical check-up for any ailment
options.C: Cancer patients travelling for treatment or periodic check-up
options.D: Only patients referred by a Government hospital for indoor treatment

e: Under the concession rules in the Coaching Tariff, cancer patients are granted fare concession when travelling for treatment or for periodic check-up, subject to the prescribed certificate and conditions.

q: A reservation clerk, while reconciling a day's bookings, has to record the length of the Passenger Name Record number allotted to each reservation in the system. The PNR number allotted to a reservation on Indian Railways is a:
e: The Passenger Name Record (PNR) allotted by the Passenger Reservation System to every reservation is a 10-digit number, which uniquely identifies the booking for enquiry and charting.

q: The owner of a private siding claims that, the siding having been provided for his traffic, the Railways should also bear the cost of maintaining it. The correct position is that the cost of maintenance of a private siding is borne by:

options.A: The Railways, as part of their ordinary working expenses
options.B: The Railways and the siding owner in equal shares in all cases
options.C: The Traffic Accounts Office of the zonal railway
options.D: The siding owner, at whose cost the siding is maintained

e: A private siding is provided for the siding owner's traffic on his own account, and under the siding agreement its maintenance is at the cost of the siding owner, not of the Railways.

q: A passenger who booked under the Tatkal scheme finds his booking status shown in the reservation system as TQWL. A junior clerk asked to expand the abbreviation for the passenger correctly states that TQWL denotes:
e: In PRS booking status codes, TQWL stands for Tatkal Quota Wait List, i.e. a waitlisted booking made against the Tatkal quota.

q: A statistics clerk is closing the monthly wagon performance return of a railway. During the month, the total wagon days on the railway were 9,60,000 and the number of wagons loaded was 2,40,000. The wagon turn-round for the month works out to:
e: Wagon turn-round is wagon days divided by wagons loaded. Here it is 9,60,000 / 2,40,000 = 4.0 days.

q: A passenger travelling by a Garib Rath Express asks the Travelling Ticket Examiner whether bedding will be supplied to him in the train and, if so, on what terms. The correct position in Garib Rath Express trains regarding bedding is that:

options.A: Bedding is not provided in these trains at all
options.B: Bedding is provided to the passengers on payment of the prescribed charges
options.C: Bedding is provided free of charge to all passengers
options.D: Bedding is provided only to passengers travelling in the air-conditioned chair car

e: In Garib Rath Express trains bedding is not included in the fare; it is supplied to passengers on payment of the prescribed charges.

q: A newly posted clerk, dealing with mail bags carried by a passenger train, assumes that the Railway Mail Service which handles the mail carried by trains is a part of the Railways' Commercial Department. The correct position is that the Railway Mail Service functions under:

options.A: The Commercial Department of the Railways
options.B: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.D: A private courier consortium engaged by the Railways

e: The Railway Mail Service, which carries and sorts mail on trains, is a part of the Department of Posts, not of the Railways; the Railways only provide the haulage and accommodation.

q: A freight customer whose traffic is urgent tells the goods clerk that he cannot wait for wagons to be supplied to him in the normal order of indents and is willing to pay extra for quicker supply. Under the Premium Indent Scheme of the Railways, such a customer can obtain:

options.A: A rebate in freight for loading traffic in the empty-flow direction
options.B: Exemption from demurrage at goods terminals
options.C: Free weighment of all his consignments
options.D: Wagons on a priority or out-of-turn basis, on payment of a premium over the normal wagon registration fee

e: Under the Premium Indent Scheme a freight customer can get wagons on priority or out-of-turn basis by paying a premium over the normal wagon registration fee, instead of waiting his turn under normal indents.

q: A divisional officer has to decide whether the superfast charge is leviable on a newly introduced train. A train is classified as a superfast train for the purpose of levy of the superfast charge when its average speed, including halts, is not less than:
e: A train is treated as superfast for levy of the superfast charge when its average speed, including halts, is 55 km per hour or more.

q: A passenger at a booking window asks for a reserved berth in an Antyodaya Express train for a long-distance journey. The clerk correctly informs him that Antyodaya Express trains are:

options.A: Premium fully air-conditioned trains with dynamic fares
options.B: Trains having only Sleeper class accommodation
options.C: Trains run exclusively for the carriage of parcels
options.D: Fully unreserved trains having general second class accommodation

e: Antyodaya Express trains are fully unreserved trains with general second class accommodation, run for the common passenger without any reserved classes.

q: A freight customer registers his demand for wagons electronically instead of visiting the goods office. In the Freight Operations Information System, the facility he has used, abbreviated as e-RD, stands for:
e: In FOIS, e-RD stands for Electronic Registration of Demand, the facility by which a customer registers his wagon demand electronically.

q: Two claimants approach a claims officer for advice on the time limits for filing their applications before the Railway Claims Tribunal. Consider the following statements: 1. A claim for compensation for the death of, or injury to, a passenger in a train accident or an untoward incident must be filed within one year of the occurrence of the accident or incident. 2. A claim for compensation for loss of, damage to or non-delivery of goods must be filed within three years. Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, a claim for death or injury in a train accident or untoward incident must be filed within one year, and a claim for loss, damage or non-delivery of goods within three years, so both statements are correct.

q: An accounts clerk preparing a note on agencies dealing with railway passengers has to expand the abbreviation IRCTC correctly. IRCTC stands for:

options.A: Indian Railway Catering and Transport Corporation
options.B: International Rail Catering and Tourism Company
options.C: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.D: Indian Rail Coach and Tourism Corporation

e: IRCTC stands for Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation, the railway PSU handling catering, tourism and online ticketing.

q: A costing officer is checking the goods performance figures of a railway which performed 84,00,000 Net Tonne Kilometres during a period in which the tonnes carried were 2,10,000. The average lead of goods traffic of the railway works out to:
e: Average lead of goods traffic is Net Tonne Kilometres divided by tonnes carried. Here it is 84,00,000 / 2,10,000 = 40 km.

q: A recipient of a gallantry award of the Chakra series applies for the facility of free travel in air-conditioned classes along with a companion. The facility extended to such recipients, entitling the holder to free travel in air-conditioned classes along with a companion, is the:
e: Recipients of Chakra series gallantry awards are granted the Complimentary Card Pass facility, entitling them to free travel in AC classes along with a companion.

q: A goods clerk has to advise a merchant whether the Busy Season Charge on goods traffic will apply to a consignment he proposes to book in the month of August. The busy season for goods traffic on Indian Railways is the period from:
e: For goods traffic the busy season on Indian Railways runs from October to June, and the Busy Season Charge is levied on traffic booked in that period, subject to notified exceptions.

q: A passenger proposes to carry, as his personal luggage in the passenger compartment, articles of a dangerous or offensive nature, saying that they are securely packed. The correct position is that such articles are:

options.A: Permitted to be carried as luggage in the brake van without any restriction
options.B: Prohibited only if they are liquids
options.C: Not permitted to be carried by a passenger as luggage in the passenger compartment
options.D: Permitted to be carried in the compartment if they are securely packed

e: Under the Railways Act and Coaching Tariff, dangerous or offensive articles are not permitted to be carried by a passenger as luggage in the passenger compartment.

q: A freight customer who has booked a consignment through the Freight Operations Information System wants to trace its position and movement while it is in transit. He can do so through the system by quoting:

options.A: The number of the wagon in which it was loaded only
options.C: The code of the siding at which it was booked
options.D: The Railway Receipt number of the consignment

e: A consignment booked through FOIS can be traced in transit through the system by quoting its Railway Receipt (RR) number.

q: A booking clerk finds that the reservation charge collected on two reserved tickets of different classes is not the same amount, and a passenger questions the difference. The correct position is that the reservation charge levied on a reserved ticket:

options.A: Varies according to the class of travel
options.B: Is uniform for all classes of travel
options.C: Is levied only on tickets in the air-conditioned classes
options.D: Is levied only on Tatkal tickets

e: The reservation charge on a reserved ticket is not uniform; it is prescribed class-wise and varies according to the class of travel.

q: A passenger wishes to book reserved accommodation well ahead of his journey, otherwise than under the Tatkal scheme, and asks the reservation clerk how far in advance booking opens. The advance reservation period for booking reserved accommodation in trains, otherwise than under the Tatkal scheme, is:
e: The advance reservation period for reserved accommodation, other than under Tatkal, is 60 days, so booking opens 60 days before the date of journey.

q: A dairy federation despatches milk from the producing centres to a metropolitan city by rail and asks the goods clerk what stock will be used for the traffic. Milk traffic from the producing centres to the metropolitan cities is carried by the Railways in:

options.D: Passenger coaches attached to mail trains

e: Milk traffic from producing centres to metropolitan cities is carried in special milk tank wagons provided for that traffic.

q: A traffic costing cell has worked out that the total cost of the coaching services of a railway for a period is Rs 33,00,000 and the passenger kilometres performed are 1,10,00,000. The cost per passenger kilometre works out to:
e: Cost per passenger kilometre is total coaching cost divided by passenger kilometres. Here it is 33,00,000 / 1,10,00,000 = Rs 0.30.

q: A patient who has to travel regularly to a hospital for dialysis treatment asks whether any concession in rail fare is admissible in his case. Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: All patients travelling to any hospital for indoor treatment
options.B: Persons accompanying a patient as attendant, in all cases
options.C: Kidney patients travelling for dialysis treatment
options.D: Patients travelling for a general health check-up

e: Under the concession rules, kidney patients travelling for dialysis treatment are granted fare concession on the prescribed conditions and certificate.

q: A consignee argues that, transit of his goods having terminated, the Railways now hold the goods merely as an insurer against all risks. In regard to the responsibility of the railway administration after the termination of transit, the correct position under the Railways Act, 1989 is that it is that of:

options.B: A bailee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872
options.C: A common carrier with absolute liability

e: Under Section 99 of the Railways Act, 1989, after termination of transit the railway administration's responsibility for the goods is that of a bailee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872.

q: A passenger's booking status in the reservation system is shown as GNWL, and he asks the enquiry clerk what the abbreviation means. In the Passenger Reservation System, GNWL stands for:
e: In PRS status codes, GNWL stands for General Wait List, the wait list against the general quota.

q: A passenger comparing fares finds that a Tejas Express charges more than a comparable Shatabdi Express for the same journey and asks why. Tejas Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Non-air-conditioned trains run for the carriage of parcels
options.C: Premium fully air-conditioned trains whose fares are higher than those of comparable Shatabdi Express trains
options.D: Trains run exclusively for the carriage of automobiles

e: Tejas Express trains are premium fully air-conditioned trains, and their fares are kept higher than those of comparable Shatabdi Express trains.

q: A loco foreman is checking a monthly return which shows that the locomotives of a railway ran 7,20,000 engine kilometres during the month and the engine days numbered 2,400. The engine kilometres per engine day work out to:
e: Engine kilometres per engine day is engine kilometres divided by engine days. Here it is 7,20,000 / 2,400 = 300.

q: A freight officer planning despatches over a newly opened freight corridor asks which organisation has built and operates the Dedicated Freight Corridors of the Railways. The Dedicated Freight Corridors have been built and are operated by:

options.A: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited
options.B: The zonal railways through which they pass

e: The Dedicated Freight Corridors have been built and are operated by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL).

q: A sports person selected to take part in a tournament asks the booking clerk whether she can get any concession in rail fare for the journey. Concession in railway fares is admissible, under the prescribed conditions, to:

options.A: Spectators travelling to witness sporting events
options.B: Owners of sports goods firms travelling on business
options.C: Retired sports persons travelling for personal purposes
options.D: Sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level

e: Fare concession is admissible to sports persons travelling to participate in tournaments at the national or State level, on production of the prescribed certificate.

q: A passenger travelling by a Rajdhani Express refuses to pay when meals served to him during the journey are, according to him, separately chargeable, and the ticket checking staff have to settle the position. The fare charged for travel by Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express trains:

options.A: Does not cover meals, which are always charged for separately
options.B: Covers meals only in Air-conditioned First Class
options.C: Is inclusive of the cost of meals served to the passengers during the journey
options.D: Is inclusive of the cost of retiring rooms at the destination station

e: The fare for Rajdhani and Shatabdi Express trains is inclusive of the cost of meals served to passengers during the journey; catering charges form part of the ticket fare.

q: At a station, a passenger obtains an unreserved ticket from a machine which prints the ticket on his pressing the destination for which he wants it. In the abbreviation SPTM, used for such machines at railway stations, SPTM stands for:
e: SPTM stands for Self Printing Ticket Machine, the machine at stations which prints an unreserved ticket when the passenger presses the destination.

q: A statistics clerk has to report the density of passenger traffic on a railway which performed 84,00,000 passenger kilometres during a year in which the route kilometres open for traffic were 4,200. The density of passenger traffic on the railway works out to:
e: Density of passenger traffic is passenger kilometres divided by route kilometres. Here it is 84,00,000 / 4,200 = 2,000 passenger kilometres per route kilometre.

q: A commuter who has shifted his residence farther away asks the booking clerk up to what distance a Monthly Season Ticket can ordinarily be issued to him. Monthly Season Tickets on Indian Railways are ordinarily issued for journeys not exceeding:
e: Monthly Season Tickets are ordinarily issued for journeys not exceeding 150 kilometres.

q: A consignor books an entire train load of his traffic from his siding to one single station and asks the goods clerk what such a formation is called in goods traffic. In goods traffic, a 'block rake' means:

options.A: A rake which is blocked for departmental use during emergencies
options.B: A full train-load consignment booked by one party from one station to a single destination station
options.C: A rake formed of wagons belonging to different owning railways
options.D: A rake detained at a station for want of movement instructions

e: A block rake is a full train-load consignment booked by one party from one station to a single destination station.

q: An accounts officer classifying accident figures for a report has to place an accident which resulted in loss of human life, damage to railway property and interruption of through traffic. Such accidents, which have serious repercussions of that kind, are classified on the Railways as:
e: Accidents with serious repercussions such as loss of human life, damage to railway property and interruption to through traffic are classified as consequential train accidents.

q: A passenger choosing between two air-conditioned classes finds that the fare for the AC Three Tier Economy class is not the same as that for AC Three Tier and asks the clerk which is cheaper. In the case of the AC Three Tier Economy class, the fare charged, as compared with the fare for AC Three Tier class, is:

options.A: Higher, because of the additional berths provided in the coaches
options.B: The same as for AC Three Tier class
options.C: Lower than that for AC Three Tier class
options.D: Higher during the peak season only

e: The fare for AC Three Tier Economy class is lower than the fare for AC Three Tier class, the class having been introduced as a cheaper AC option.

q: A passenger at a station sees a long-distance train with locomotives attached at both ends and non-air-conditioned coaches, meant for affordable long-distance travel. Such trains, worked on the push-pull principle with locomotives at both ends, are the:

options.A: Premium fully air-conditioned trains with dynamic fares
options.C: Suburban EMU services run in metropolitan cities
options.D: Tourist trains run exclusively for foreign tourists

e: Trains worked on the push-pull principle with locomotives at both ends and non-AC coaches for affordable long-distance travel are the Amrit Bharat Express trains.

q: A passenger who has a grievance about the amenities at a station asks where he can formally record it for the attention of the railway administration. For this purpose, at every station of the Railways there is maintained a:

options.A: Register of inspection remarks of the Travelling Inspector of Accounts
options.B: Record of the results of internal check by the Accounts Department
options.C: Register of complaints by the station staff against passengers
options.D: Complaint book, in which passengers can record their complaints and suggestions

e: A complaint book is maintained at every station in which passengers can record their complaints and suggestions for the attention of the administration.

q: A tourist travelling on a scenic route finds that his coach has large glass windows and a glass roof through which he can view the scenery along the route. Such coaches provided on certain trains of Indian Railways are:

options.B: Air-conditioned executive-class coaches with on-board catering
options.D: Sleeper coaches fitted with individual entertainment screens

e: Coaches with large glass windows and a glass roof for viewing scenery on scenic routes are Vistadome coaches.

q: A commuter on a main line section travels by a short-distance electric multiple unit service and asks the clerk what such trains are called. MEMU trains on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Diesel multiple unit trains run on unelectrified branch lines
options.B: Trains hauled by battery-operated locomotives in yards
options.C: Electric multiple unit trains run for short and medium distance services on main lines
options.D: Inspection trains run for track-recording purposes

e: MEMU trains are electric multiple unit trains run for short and medium distance services on main line sections.

q: A container operator tells a freight officer that on one corridor his containers are carried stacked two high on the wagons, and the officer has to identify the corridor in his report. Double-stack container trains, in which containers are carried stacked two high on wagons, are operated on Indian Railways on the:

options.C: Metre-gauge sections of the North Eastern Railway

e: Double-stack container trains, with containers stacked two high on wagons, are operated on the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, which is built to that loading standard.

q: A passenger with a limited budget asks at a station where he can get an economical, wholesome meal, and is directed to an outlet run for that purpose. 'Jan Aahar' outlets at railway stations are run by the Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation to provide:

options.A: Packaged drinking water at controlled prices
options.B: Economical, low-priced wholesome meals to the travelling public
options.D: Refreshment rooms on lease to private caterers

e: Jan Aahar outlets are run by IRCTC at stations to provide economical, low-priced wholesome meals to the travelling public.

q: A passenger planning a long-distance journey of more than 200 kilometres by an unreserved train asks the booking clerk how far ahead he can buy his unreserved ticket. Advance booking of unreserved tickets for such long-distance journeys is permitted at stations and through the Unreserved Ticketing System:

options.A: Up to 7 days in advance for all journeys
options.B: Only on the day of the journey
options.C: Up to 3 days in advance, where the distance of the journey exceeds 200 kilometres
options.D: Up to 30 days in advance for all journeys

e: Advance booking of unreserved tickets through UTS is permitted up to 3 days in advance where the journey distance exceeds 200 kilometres; for shorter journeys it is the day of journey only.

q: A passenger who does not want to queue at a reservation office gets his reserved ticket booked through an agent outside the station and pays him a service charge besides the fare. Such agents, licensed by the Railways to book reserved tickets on behalf of passengers on charging a prescribed service charge, are:

options.A: Agents authorised to sell unreserved tickets at halt stations
options.C: Contractors engaged for loading and unloading of goods at stations
options.D: Staff deputed by travel agencies to work at reservation counters

e: Agents licensed by the Railways to book reserved tickets for passengers on a prescribed service charge are Rail Travellers' Service Agents (RTSAs).

q: A station accountant is closing the monthly Station Balance Sheet. The opening outstanding balance of the month was Rs 3,60,000, the earnings and other debits of the month were Rs 12,40,000, and the remittances and other credits of the month were Rs 13,50,000. The closing outstanding balance of the month works out to:
e: Closing outstanding equals opening outstanding plus debits minus credits: 3,60,000 + 12,40,000 - 13,50,000 = Rs 2,50,000.

q: On a morning round, the station cashier finds that the previous day's station earnings have been collected from the station premises itself by the authorised bank and deposited directly into the Railways' bank account, without the station staff carrying the cash anywhere. This arrangement for the remittance of station earnings is known as:
e: Collection of station earnings from the station premises by the authorised bank, credited directly to the Railways' bank account, is door-step banking.

q: A man who is neither a railway servant nor an authorised agent is found unauthorisedly carrying on the business of procuring and supplying railway tickets to passengers for profit. Such unauthorised carrying on of the business of procuring and supplying railway tickets (touting) is punishable under:
e: Unauthorised carrying on of the business of procuring and supplying railway tickets (touting) is punishable under Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989.

q: A costing officer is verifying a loco shed's monthly return, which shows that the goods locomotives consumed 6,300 litres of diesel oil during the month while performing 18,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. On verification, the Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of the railway for the month works out to:
e: Specific Fuel Consumption is fuel consumed per 1000 GTKM. Here it is 6,300 / (18,00,000 / 1000) = 6,300 / 1,800 = 3.5 litres per 1000 GTKM.

q: A person enters the railway premises without lawful authority and refuses to leave the premises when asked to do so by the railway staff. Trespass upon railway premises, and refusal to leave the premises when requested to do so, is punishable under:
e: Trespass on railway premises and refusal to leave when asked to do so is punishable under Section 147 of the Railways Act, 1989.

q: At an occupancy review, a division reports that against 80,00,000 seat kilometres offered during the period, its coaching services actually performed 44,00,000 passenger kilometres. The load factor (occupation ratio) reported for the coaching services is:
e: Load factor is passenger kilometres divided by seat kilometres offered, as a percentage. Here it is 44,00,000 / 80,00,000 x 100 = 55 per cent.

q: A bulk consumer invests in general purpose wagons, which are inducted into service on the Railways, and loads his traffic in such wagons. Under the General Purpose Wagon Investment Scheme (GPWIS) of the Railways, the customer so investing is granted, for the traffic loaded in such wagons:

options.A: Exemption from demurrage at all terminals
options.C: Free weighment of all his consignments
options.D: Ownership of the track on which the wagons run

e: Under the General Purpose Wagon Investment Scheme (GPWIS), a customer who invests in general purpose wagons inducted into service gets a rebate in freight on traffic loaded in those wagons.

q: The passenger earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 1,12,00,000 and the number of passengers carried during the period is 28,00,000. The earnings per passenger of the railway for the period are:
e: Earnings per passenger is passenger earnings divided by passengers carried. Here it is 1,12,00,000 / 28,00,000 = Rs 4.

q: A private operator invests in specially designed wagons for the carriage of automobiles and runs automobile traffic in them over the railway network. Under the Automobile Freight Train Operator (AFTO) scheme of the Railways, the operator so investing pays to the Railways, for the movement of his wagons over the network:

options.B: Only the licence fee for the terminal used
options.C: Passenger fares for the staff accompanying the wagons

e: Under the Automobile Freight Train Operator (AFTO) scheme, the investing operator pays haulage charges to the Railways for movement of his automobile wagons over the network.

q: A finance officer is reviewing the annual results of a zonal railway whose gross earnings for the year are Rs 5,000 crore and whose working expenses are Rs 4,800 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway for the year works out to:
e: Operating Ratio is working expenses as a percentage of gross earnings. Here it is 4800 / 5000 x 100 = 96 per cent.

q: A passenger at a station wants to know whether his train is running late and by how much, without approaching the enquiry counter. The system of Indian Railways which primarily provides real-time information about the running of trains for the travelling public is the:
e: Real-time train running information for the travelling public is provided primarily through the National Train Enquiry System (NTES).

q: A statistics clerk is closing the monthly wagon performance return of a railway. During the month, the total wagon days on the railway were 7,50,000 and the number of wagons loaded was 3,00,000. The wagon turn-round for the month works out to:
e: Wagon turn-round is wagon days divided by wagons loaded. Here it is 7,50,000 / 3,00,000 = 2.5 days.

q: A passenger who has a complaint about catering in a train, and another who needs assistance during his journey, are both directed to a single integrated facility of Indian Railways for registration, tracking and resolution of passenger complaints and grievances. This facility is:
e: Rail Madad is the single integrated facility of Indian Railways for registration, tracking and resolution of passenger complaints and grievances, including catering complaints and journey assistance.

q: A costing officer has to work out the average lead of the goods traffic of a railway which performed 1,26,00,000 Net Tonne Kilometres during a period in which the tonnes carried were 2,80,000. The average lead of goods traffic of the railway works out to:
e: Average lead of goods traffic is Net Tonne Kilometres divided by tonnes carried. Here it is 1,26,00,000 / 2,80,000 = 45 km.

q: An accounts clerk has to classify, in the books of a zonal railway, a large amount received from the sale of unserviceable and surplus assets of the railway. The correct position in regard to this amount is that it:

options.A: Forms part of the coaching earnings of the railway
options.B: Forms part of the goods earnings of the railway
options.C: Does not form part of the gross traffic earnings of the railway
options.D: Forms part of the sundry other earnings of the railway

e: Amounts from sale of unserviceable and surplus assets are capital or miscellaneous receipts, not traffic earnings; they do not form part of the gross traffic earnings of the railway.

q: A passenger books a paperless ticket through the UTS mobile application and, during checking, produces a screenshot of the ticket saved in the photo gallery of his phone. The correct position in regard to a paperless ticket booked through the UTS mobile application is that:

options.A: The screenshot of the ticket is accepted as a valid ticket during checking
options.B: Only a printout of the ticket is accepted during checking
options.C: The ticket must be shown on the mobile handset through the application itself, and a printout or screenshot of it is not accepted as a valid ticket
options.D: The ticket can be transferred to another passenger's handset before the journey

e: A paperless UTS mobile ticket must be shown on the handset through the UTS application itself; a screenshot or printout of it is not accepted as a valid ticket during checking.

q: A traffic costing cell has worked out that the total cost of the coaching services of a railway for a period is Rs 52,50,000 and the passenger kilometres performed are 1,05,00,000. The cost per passenger kilometre works out to:
e: Cost per passenger kilometre is total coaching cost divided by passenger kilometres. Here it is 52,50,000 / 1,05,00,000 = Rs 0.50.

q: A statistics officer is compiling the operating statistics of Indian Railways as a whole from the returns of the zonal railways. For this compilation, the operating statistics of Indian Railways are compiled:

options.A: Only for the Broad Gauge system
options.B: For all gauges together in a single combined statement
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year
options.D: Separately for the Broad Gauge, Metre Gauge and Narrow Gauge systems

e: The operating statistics of Indian Railways are compiled separately for the Broad Gauge, Metre Gauge and Narrow Gauge systems, and not as one combined statement for all gauges.

q: A loco foreman compares two utilisation indices of his shed: engine kilometres per engine day on line and engine kilometres per engine day in use. Engine kilometres per engine day in use is regarded as the sharper index of locomotive utilisation because it:

options.A: Excludes the engines which are under repair, spare or otherwise not actually working
options.B: Includes the shunting kilometres of all the yards of the railway
options.C: Is computed only for electric locomotives of the shed
options.D: Is based on the number of trains run rather than on the engines

e: Engine kilometres per engine day in use is the sharper utilisation index because its denominator excludes engines under repair, spare or otherwise not actually working.

q: A loco foreman is checking a monthly return which shows that the locomotives of a railway ran 11,55,000 engine kilometres during the month and the engine days numbered 3,300. The engine kilometres per engine day work out to:
e: Engine kilometres per engine day is engine kilometres divided by engine days. Here it is 11,55,000 / 3,300 = 350.

q: A railway employee, travelling with his family where admissible, books a journey on a Privilege Ticket Order (PTO) issued to him. For travel on a Privilege Ticket Order, the employee is required to pay:
e: On a Privilege Ticket Order (PTO), a railway employee pays one-third of the public fare for the journey.

q: A statistics clerk has to report the density of passenger traffic on a railway which performed 1,25,00,000 passenger kilometres during a year in which the route kilometres open for traffic were 5,000. The density of passenger traffic on the railway works out to:
e: Density of passenger traffic is passenger kilometres divided by route kilometres. Here it is 1,25,00,000 / 5,000 = 2,500 passenger kilometres per route kilometre.

q: A tourist books a round tour which begins and ends at the same station, the outward journey and the return journey being performed by different routes. The ticket issued for such a round tour is a:
e: A ticket for a round tour beginning and ending at the same station, with outward and return journeys by different routes, is a circular journey ticket.

q: The statistical cell of a zonal railway has to report the total track kilometres of a section whose route length is 80 kilometres, laid with two running lines throughout, and which has, in addition, 24 kilometres of sidings, yard lines and other tracks. Counting each line separately, as track kilometres are counted, the total track kilometres of the section work out to:
e: Track kilometres count each running line separately, plus sidings and yard lines. Here it is 80 x 2 + 24 = 184 kilometres.

q: A passenger in difficulty during a journey is advised by the ticket checking staff to seek help on the integrated helpline number of Indian Railways for passenger enquiries, assistance and Rail Madad services. This integrated helpline number is:
e: The integrated helpline number of Indian Railways for passenger enquiries, assistance and Rail Madad services is 139.

q: During a month, the locomotives in electric traction on a railway consumed 90,000 kWh of electrical energy and performed 36,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) of the railway for the month works out to:
e: Specific Energy Consumption is energy consumed per 1000 GTKM. Here it is 90,000 / (36,00,000 / 1000) = 90,000 / 3,600 = 25 kWh per 1000 GTKM.

q: A passenger books a berth in a Humsafar Express train and asks the booking clerk what classes of accommodation the train carries. Humsafar Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Fully unreserved trains for short-distance travel
options.B: Fully air-conditioned trains having only AC 3-tier accommodation
options.C: Trains having only air-conditioned chair car accommodation
options.D: Trains having a mixture of AC and non-AC classes

e: Humsafar Express trains are fully air-conditioned trains having only AC 3-tier accommodation.

q: A performance analyst has to work out the Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day of a railway which performed 45,50,000 Net Tonne Kilometres during a period in which the goods engine days numbered 1,300. The Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day work out to:
e: Net Tonne Kilometres per engine day is NTKM divided by goods engine days. Here it is 45,50,000 / 1,300 = 3,500.

q: The electrical engineer of a zonal railway has to account for the total electrical energy consumed on the railway during a month, for which separate figures are available for the energy used in hauling trains and for the energy used for other purposes such as lighting and workshops. The electrical energy consumed on a railway is accounted for separately as:

options.A: Traction consumption only, the other consumption being ignored
options.B: A single combined figure for all purposes together

e: Electrical energy consumed on a railway is accounted for separately as traction consumption (hauling trains) and non-traction consumption (lighting, workshops and other purposes).

q: A trader complains to the railway administration that the rate charged on his traffic is unreasonable, and is advised that the functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal, which dealt with complaints regarding the reasonableness of the rates charged by the Railways, now vest in the:
e: The functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal, which heard complaints about the reasonableness of rates charged, now vest in the Railway Claims Tribunal.

q: The gross earnings of a railway for a period are Rs 2,70,00,000. During the same period it performed 45,00,000 passenger kilometres and 90,00,000 Net Tonne Kilometres. The earnings per traffic unit of the railway work out to:
e: A traffic unit is one passenger kilometre plus one Net Tonne Kilometre, i.e. 45,00,000 + 90,00,000 = 1,35,00,000 units. Earnings per traffic unit = 2,70,00,000 / 1,35,00,000 = Rs 2.00.

q: A passenger's booking status in the reservation system is shown as PQWL, and he asks the enquiry clerk what the status means. In the Passenger Reservation System, the Pooled Quota Wait List (PQWL) applies to:

options.A: Passengers who have booked under the Tatkal scheme only
options.B: Passengers boarding at stations which share a common pooled quota for the train
options.C: Passengers boarding at the originating station of the train only
options.D: Passengers who hold season tickets for the section

e: PQWL, the Pooled Quota Wait List, applies to passengers boarding at stations which share a common pooled quota for the train.

q: A wagon is detained at a goods terminal well beyond the free time allowed for its unloading, and the detention continues for several more days. Demurrage charges for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed are levied:

options.A: At a flat rate for all periods of detention
options.B: Only for the first day of detention
options.C: At rates which decrease as the period of detention lengthens
options.D: At rates which increase (escalate) as the period of detention lengthens

e: Demurrage for detention of wagons beyond free time is levied at slab rates which increase (escalate) as the period of detention lengthens, to discourage detention.

q: A parcel clerk accepts a parcel for booking and is asked by the consignor whether the charges can be paid by the consignee on delivery, as in 'to-pay' goods traffic. In parcel traffic, the correct position is that the parcel charges are:

options.A: Required to be prepaid at the time of booking
options.B: Always collected at the destination station as 'to-pay' charges
options.C: Billed to the consignee month by month
options.D: Recovered only after weighment of the parcel at the destination

e: In parcel traffic, the charges are required to be prepaid at the time of booking; parcels are not booked on a to-pay basis like goods.

q: A goods clerk explains to a consignor why the freight rate per tonne kilometre quoted for his long-distance consignment is lower than the rate per tonne kilometre for a short-distance consignment of the same commodity. Goods class rates on the Railways are framed on the basis that:

options.A: The rate per tonne kilometre tapers (decreases) as the distance of carriage increases, on the telescopic principle
options.B: The rate per tonne kilometre is charged at a flat rate, irrespective of the distance of carriage
options.C: The rate per tonne kilometre increases as the distance of carriage increases
options.D: A single rate applies to all distances up to the maximum lead of the railway

e: Goods class rates are framed on the telescopic principle, under which the rate per tonne kilometre tapers, i.e. decreases, as the distance of carriage increases.

q: At a station, the booking clerk collects money from visitors for the sale of platform tickets issued during the day, and the accounts clerk has to classify the amount in the earnings of the Railways. Receipts from the sale of platform tickets at stations form part of:
e: Receipts from sale of platform tickets are classified under coaching earnings of the Railways.

q: A booking clerk spoils a printed ticket before it can be issued to any passenger, and cancels another ticket before issue on the passenger changing his mind. In regard to such tickets which are spoiled or cancelled before issue, the correct position is that they:

options.A: Are destroyed at the station itself and are not required to be accounted for
options.B: Are also returned by the station as non-issued tickets and must be fully accounted for
options.C: Are sold later to other passengers at a discount
options.D: Are accounted for only at the close of the financial year

e: Tickets spoiled or cancelled before issue are also returned by the station as non-issued tickets and must be fully accounted for in the station accounts.

q: Floods followed by a strike bring goods working at a group of stations to a standstill, and large demurrage accrues against parties for detentions which were beyond their control. In such exceptional circumstances, a general remission of demurrage for a station or an area can be granted:

options.A: By the goods clerk on duty on his own authority
options.B: By the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during his inspection
options.C: Automatically, without any orders, on the expiry of the free time
options.D: Under the orders of the competent authority

e: A general remission of demurrage for a station or an area in exceptional circumstances such as floods and strikes can be granted only under the orders of the competent authority.

q: During a period, the total wagon kilometres run on a railway were 1,10,00,000, of which the empty wagon kilometres were 49,50,000. The percentage of empty wagon kilometres to total wagon kilometres is:
e: Percentage of empty wagon kilometres is empty wagon kilometres divided by total wagon kilometres. Here it is 49,50,000 / 1,10,00,000 x 100 = 45 per cent.

q: A passenger approaches the reservation counter one morning to book a Tatkal ticket for a journey on the following day. Tatkal tickets are opened for booking:

options.A: Seven days in advance of the date of journey
options.B: Two days in advance of the date of journey
options.C: One day in advance of the date of journey
options.D: Ten days in advance of the date of journey

e: Tatkal tickets open for booking one day in advance of the date of journey.

q: A container operator tenders a consignment measured in Forty-foot Equivalent Units (FEUs) and the goods clerk has to record the traffic in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs). One Forty-foot Equivalent Unit (FEU) in container traffic is equal to:
e: One Forty-foot Equivalent Unit (FEU) equals two Twenty-foot Equivalent Units, i.e. 2 TEUs, a forty-foot container counting as two twenty-foot units.

q: A student holding a concession certificate asks the booking clerk whether the concession in fare admissible to him on ordinary tickets will also be allowed on a Tatkal ticket which he proposes to book. In the case of Tatkal tickets, the position regarding concessions in fare is that:

options.A: All concessions admissible on ordinary tickets are also admissible on Tatkal tickets
options.B: Concession is admissible only to students on Tatkal tickets
options.C: Concession is admissible only to senior citizens on Tatkal tickets
options.D: No concession is admissible on Tatkal tickets

e: No fare concession of any kind is admissible on Tatkal tickets, even if the passenger is otherwise eligible for concession on ordinary tickets.

q: A railway performed 78,00,000 passenger kilometres during a period in which the passenger train kilometres run were 15,600. The average number of passengers carried per train is:
e: Average passengers per train is passenger kilometres divided by passenger train kilometres. Here it is 78,00,000 / 15,600 = 500.

q: A group of students travels on an educational tour sponsored by a recognised educational institution, producing the prescribed concession certificate issued by the institution. Students so travelling in a group on an educational tour are entitled to:

options.A: Free travel in all classes of trains
options.B: Concession only in the unreserved classes
options.C: Concession in rail fares, on production of the prescribed concession certificate/form from the institution

e: Students travelling in a group on an educational tour sponsored by a recognised institution get concession in rail fares on production of the prescribed concession certificate or form from the institution.

q: A departmental material train carrying rails and sleepers for the Railways' own works is run over a section along with the ordinary traffic trains. In railway statistics, trains run for such departmental purposes, carrying railway materials for the Railways' own use, are classified as:
e: Trains run for departmental purposes carrying railway material for the Railways' own use are classified in statistics as departmental (non-revenue) trains, not revenue-earning trains.

q: A station accountant is closing the monthly Station Balance Sheet. The opening outstanding balance of the month was Rs 4,20,000, the earnings and other debits of the month were Rs 15,30,000, and the remittances and other credits of the month were Rs 17,10,000. The closing outstanding balance of the month works out to:
e: Closing outstanding equals opening outstanding plus debits minus credits: 4,20,000 + 15,30,000 - 17,10,000 = Rs 2,40,000.

q: The statistical cell of a zonal railway has to report the total track kilometres of a section whose route length is 65 kilometres, laid with two running lines throughout, and which has, in addition, 18 kilometres of sidings, yard lines and other tracks. Counting each line separately, as track kilometres are counted, the total track kilometres of the section work out to:
e: Track kilometres count each running line separately, plus sidings and yard lines. Here it is 65 x 2 + 18 = 148 kilometres.

q: A costing officer is verifying a loco shed's monthly return, which shows that the goods locomotives consumed 9,600 litres of diesel oil during the month while performing 24,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. On verification, the Specific Fuel Consumption (SFC) of the railway for the month works out to:
e: Specific Fuel Consumption is fuel per 1000 GTKM. Here it is 9,600 / (24,00,000 / 1000) = 9,600 / 2,400 = 4.0 litres per 1000 GTKM.

q: During a month, the locomotives in electric traction on a railway consumed 1,20,000 kWh of electrical energy and performed 40,00,000 Gross Tonne Kilometres. The Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) of the railway for the month works out to:
e: Specific Energy Consumption is energy per 1000 GTKM. Here it is 1,20,000 / (40,00,000 / 1000) = 1,20,000 / 4,000 = 30 kWh per 1000 GTKM.

q: At an occupancy review, a division reports that against 90,00,000 seat kilometres offered during the period, its coaching services actually performed 63,00,000 passenger kilometres. The load factor (occupation ratio) reported for the coaching services is:
e: Load factor is passenger kilometres divided by seat kilometres offered. Here it is 63,00,000 / 90,00,000 x 100 = 70 per cent.

q: A finance officer is reviewing the annual results of a zonal railway whose gross earnings for the year are Rs 5,000 crore and whose working expenses are Rs 4,550 crore. The Operating Ratio of the railway for the year works out to:
e: Operating Ratio is working expenses as a percentage of gross earnings. Here it is 4550 / 5000 x 100 = 91 per cent.

q: A statistics clerk is closing the monthly wagon performance return of a railway. During the month, the total wagon days on the railway were 9,80,000 and the number of wagons loaded was 2,80,000. The wagon turn-round for the month works out to:
e: Wagon turn-round is wagon days divided by wagons loaded. Here it is 9,80,000 / 2,80,000 = 3.5 days.

q: A costing officer has to work out the average lead of the goods traffic of a railway which performed 1,54,00,000 Net Tonne Kilometres during a period in which the tonnes carried were 2,80,000. The average lead of goods traffic of the railway works out to:
e: Average lead of goods traffic is Net Tonne Kilometres divided by tonnes carried. Here it is 1,54,00,000 / 2,80,000 = 55 km.

q: A traffic costing cell has worked out that the total cost of the coaching services of a railway for a period is Rs 66,00,000 and the passenger kilometres performed are 1,20,00,000. The cost per passenger kilometre works out to:
e: Cost per passenger kilometre is total coaching cost divided by passenger kilometres. Here it is 66,00,000 / 1,20,00,000 = Rs 0.55.

q: A loco foreman is checking a monthly return which shows that the locomotives of a railway ran 14,40,000 engine kilometres during the month and the engine days numbered 4,000. The engine kilometres per engine day work out to:
e: Engine kilometres per engine day is engine kilometres divided by engine days. Here it is 14,40,000 / 4,000 = 360.
